1  JUDGMENT

The present petition is filed under Sec.166 of MV Act 1989 by injured minor petitioner through his natural guardian seeking compensation of .20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
2. It is case of the petitioner is that: on 17.04.2023 at about 12.55 p.m. when petitioner was standing in front of Aishwarya Bakery, Near Sandeep Unnikrishnan road, Chikkabetta Halli.
The rider of a pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-X-6577 (herein after called as offending vehicle) rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries all over her body.
She was Immediately shifted to Prasad Global Hospital, where, she has taken treatment as an inpatient and incurred .2,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.
The accident occurred due rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle.
3. At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 12 years and was a student.
Due to the injuries sustained, he was unable to attend the school or participate in curricular and extra curricular activities, which has adversely affected his education and future prospects.

4. The Petitioner claims that the Respondents, being the owner and insurer of the alleged offending vehicle, jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest for injuries, pain suffering and financial loss caused by the accident.
5. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.

6. The Respondent No.1-RC owner has filed his written statement denying the averments made in the petition inter alia contending that accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and she was the responsible for the accident.
He stated that he is the owner of the offending vehicle, and that it was duly insured insurance with the Respondent No.2. the insurance policy was valid as on the date of accident.

It is further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exaggerated, and hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
7.

The Respondent No.2-Insurance company has filed its written statement denying the averments made in the petition inter alia admitting the issuance of an insurance policy in respect of alleged offending vehicle , this respondent has disputed the validity as on the date of accident.
It has further contended that its liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent has also alleged that the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.
It has further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective permit and FC as on the date of accident.
This Respondent has denied the occurrence of the alleged accident as well as the involvement of the offending vehicle.
It is alleged that the petitioner, in active collusion with the police, has falsely implicated the offending vehicle with an intention to make unlawful gain.

It has denied the nature and extent of injuries allegedly sustained by the Petitioner, the treatment undertaken, the expenses incurred and disability Alfiya vs Vinay B.S on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150939180/
2 suffered.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.
For all these reasons, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of the above, the following Issues arise for my consideration :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in an accident when she was standing infront of Aishwarya Bakery on 17.04.2023 at about 12-55 p.m., infront of Aishwarya Bakery, Sandeep Unnikrishnan road, Chikkabetahalli, Benglauru District, due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of Pulsar motorcycle bearing number KA-50-X- 6577?

2. What compensation petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?

Additional issue:
1. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by Respondent 1 and the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
9.

In order to prove the claim, the natural guardian/mother of Petitioner is examined as PW.1, the medical record officer at Prasad Global Hospital is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P-20.
On the other hand The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
10. I have heard the counsel for Petitioner and perused the material on record.

11. By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Addl.Issue No.1: In the Negative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1:- Since the Petitioner being minor, represented by her natural guardian/mother and she is examined as PW-1. PW-1 has stated in her chief-examination affidavit that the accident occurred due to negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.

Further she has stated that on 17.04.2023 at about 12.55 p.m. when her daughter was standing in front of Aishwarya Bakery, Near Sandeep Unnikrishnan road, Chikkabetta Hall, the rider of pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-X-6577 was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries all over her body.

Alfiya vs Vinay B.S on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150939180/
3 13.
The grand father had given the first information statement to the Police as per Ex.P.2 on the basis of which Ex.P.1 FIR was registered.
Ex.P2 is the complaint.
Spot Mahazar and sketch was done by the Police as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
The offending vehicle was inspected as per IMV report at Ex.P5 and after completion of investigation, charge sheet is filed by the concerned Police as per Ex.P.7.
Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate, which shows that the Petitioner has sustained displaced fracture of shaft of right tibia, lacerated wound over the dorsolateral aspect of right forearm.
14. The Respondent-Insurance company has denied the occurrence of the alleged accident as well as involvement of the offending vehicle.
It is alleged that the petitioner, in active collusion with the police, has falsely implicated the offending vehicle with intention to make unlawful gain.
Except these contention, Respondent no 2 has not produced any other material before this court.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged.
All the evidence and materials clearly indicates that it was negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-
The respondent No.2 has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent no 2 has not chosen to lead positive evidence that its company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Whatever, the contention raised by the Respondent no.2 in his written statement remains as pleading only.
They have not proved by the Respondent no 2.
It is settled principle of law that the allegation of the fact can be proved by providing evidence or by eliciting something from the mouth of the opponent.
Keeping in view of modes of proving an allegation of fact, again say that the Respondent no 2 has failed to prove his contention.
The offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, hence fastening joint liability on the Respondent no 2-insurance company
Wherefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answer this issue in the negative.

16. ISSUE NO.3 :-The Petitioner was of 12 years old at the time of accident and she has sustained displaced fracture of the shaft of the right tibia, a laceration over the dorsolateral aspects of right forearm and multiple injuries to other parts of the body.
She was admitted to Prasad Global Hospital, wherein she was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries she was not able to attend her classes for considerable period.
17. PW-2, the Medical Record Officer at Prasad Global Hospital, stated that he does not have any personal knowledge with regard to Ex.P18 to Ex.P20.

He further deposed that the petitioner was initially brought to their hospital but he did not know whether the petitioner was conscious or not at Alfiya vs Vinay B.S on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150939180/
4 time of admission.
He stated that he was unaware of whether the vehicle number was mentioned in MLC or not.

PW-2 has produced MLC register extract, copy of police intimation, cash sheet report at Ex.P.18 to 20.
18.
There is no materials on record to establish that the Petitioner has suffered any loss to her educational career as a result of the accident.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
19. The PW1 has stated that she has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.
In this regard she has produced the medical bills at Ex.P.13 amounting to Rs.77,235/-.
It appears that PW1 has incurred Rs 77,235 towards medical expenses.
20. On perusal of EX P12 it appears that the petitioner has underwent surgery.
There is no doubt that the petitioner sustained a fracture to her right tibia.
However, she has not examined the doctor to establish that she has suffered any permanent disability.

Nevertheless, considering the grievous nature of the injury and in the absence of medical evidence specifically quantifying disability, this tribunal is of view that the petitioner must have endured considerable pain and suffering.

Taking into account her young age and the physical and emotional distress caused by the injury, this court deems it appropriate to award global compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.
21.
Liability:
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

22. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of .2,00,000/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank till she attains the age of majority or for a period of 2 years whichever is later.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
